proof:
For $T_H>0$, the weights $T_{Hz}/T_H$ have base mean $p$ by the capwise balance. Convexity of the actual ambient body gives $\sum_z(T_{Hz}/T_H)K_z\subseteq K_p$. Support functions are additive under Minkowski summation, proving $S_H\ge0$. For $T_H=0$ all terms vanish. For a nonzero section coarea the through-mark condition gives $\tau_z=u\cdot y+a\cdot(p-z)$, so summation gives $\sum_zG_{Hz}=\sum_zT_{Hz}h_{K_z}(u)-T_Hu\cdot y$. Substituting $S_H$ gives the formula even before integration.

The first family is actual since the lifted hull of the three boxes has exactly those fibers: the endpoint average is contained in the middle box. The second is the actual product of the base interval with the cube. Both are centrally symmetric. Every halfspace containing the mixed origin captures at least half by reflection, and opposite nonvertical through-mark cuts at any mark partition volume up to a null plane, so no mark has larger depth. The chosen pairs have half the volume at zero. In the first family, all three proper sections have coarea one and continuous mean zero, their bases average to zero, and the two opposite normals balance. The signed supports have values $1/2,1,1/2$, so the weighted support sum is two and the own support term is three. Thus $S_H=1$ and $\sum_zD_{Hz}=2d-2$.

In the identical-cube family the positive cap is outside supporting at $z=-1$, inside supporting at $z=1$, and proper at zero. At the outside support give its boundary selector value $\gamma$, and at the inside support give it $1-\gamma$, with the complementary choices for the negative cap. The two endpoint sections have opposite full means and identical allocated coareas $\gamma$. The middle section has mean zero and coarea one. Thus the balance holds. The outside height is zero, the inside height is one and the middle height is $1/2$. This gives the asserted cone sum, while the volumes are zero, one and $1/2$ in the respective statuses. In both examples the opposite selectors add to one on the whole old boundary away from section sets of surface measure zero, and the coincident facet allocations in the second example also add to one. This proves the stated selected-boundary mean with the same allocations used in the pyramid formulas.

statement:
In the labeled pyramid identity with the exact cancellation conditions, suppose $p$ is a sampled base of a convex body with actual fibers $K_z$, and put
$$
S_H=T_H h_{K_p}(u)-\sum_zT_{Hz}h_{K_z}(u).
$$
Then $S_H\ge0$ and the common cap volume satisfies
$$
dQ=\int T_H h_{K_p-y}(u)\,d\theta-\int S_H\,d\theta+\int\sum_zD_{Hz}\,d\theta.
$$
The following are equal-weight opposite critical-cap laws at the mixed origin, with all allocated section means zero and selected original-boundary mean $1/2$.
1. At bases $-1,0,1$, take unit centered cubes at the endpoints and take $[-1,1]\times[-1/2,1/2]^{d-1}$ in the middle. For the cuts $\pm X_1\ge0$, each cap has $Q=2$, $T_H=3$, $S_H=1$, and $\sum_zD_{Hz}=2d-2$. In $d=1$ this gives $dQ<T_H h_{K_p}(u)$.
2. At the same bases take three identical unit centered cubes. For the cuts $\pm(z/2+X_1)\ge0$, allocate coarea fraction $\gamma\in[0,1]$ at both end supporting facets and full coarea on the middle section. Each cap has $Q=3/2$, $T_H=1+2\gamma$, $\sum_zG_{Hz}=1/2+\gamma$, and $\sum_zD_{Hz}=3d/2-1/2-\gamma$.
title: Actual labeled pyramid deficit and two exact symmetric box laws
